meta.check_allowlist: years 1900 to 2100 and 6-digit PIN codes (not after Rs, INR or a currency sign), clock times (H:MM), dates (next to a month name, 2026-11-21, 21/11/2026), list markers at a line start, identifiers (a letter before the number: WP11, v0.2, D044; ordinal or model suffix: 3rd, 1b), commit hashes, real paths and URLs (http(s)://, /, ./, ../, ~/, or a file extension), citations (page, row, table, figure, section, no. or # with an integer and no unit), demo ordinals (card, step, beat, option or rank with one or two digits and no unit), emergency numbers 102, 108 and 112; lines with findings:skip. Durations, money and glued units (45 minutes, Rs.2000, 250mg) are scanned
meta.check_note: --check is a token guard, not a context check: a number passes when some finding with the same value and unit (km, ms, %) exists, and an 'X of Y' or 'X/Y' ratio passes when both numbers come from one group. It cannot tell which finding a sentence means; name it with {{key}} and use --strict for captions that matter

emoc drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (cited): Cited: the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery's 2-hour access indicator (share of people within 2 hours of a facility that can do caesarean section, laparotomy and treatment of open fracture). Holmer et al. 2019, Br J Surg, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6790969, note that it "does not capture whether patients actually receive care".

trauma drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (cited): Cited: the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery's 2-hour access indicator (share of people within 2 hours of a facility that can do caesarean section, laparotomy and treatment of open fracture). Holmer et al. 2019, Br J Surg, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6790969, note that it "does not capture whether patients actually receive care".

cath_lab drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice informed by ESC 2023, which sets "an absolute time of 120 min from STEMI diagnosis to PCI-mediated reperfusion" (https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/44/38/3720/7243210). The 90-minute travel window inside that is ours, not ESC's.

neurosurgery drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice informed by Seelig et al. 1981 (N Engl J Med): comatose patients with an acute subdural haematoma did much better when operated within 4 hours of injury. The 2.5-hour travel window is ours.

dialysis drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice informed by DOPPS (Moist et al. 2008, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol): longer travel time to dialysis went with worse quality of life, adherence and survival. Dialysis is repeated two or three times a week, so the window is short. The 60 minutes is ours.

icu drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; set equal to the 2-hour emergency indicator.

nicu drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; set equal to the 2-hour emergency indicator.

ct drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; set equal to the 2-hour emergency indicator.
mri drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; MRI is usually planned, so 3 hours.

burns drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; specialist burn units are few, so 4 hours.

cardiac_surgery drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; heart surgery is usually planned, so 4 hours.

oncology drive-time window, a planning threshold not a clinical deadline (design choice): Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; cancer treatment is planned and repeated, so 4 hours.
